channel.title: AI News Radar
channel.description: A curated 24-hour radar of AI news: official releases, new models and high-signal discussion.

item.title: OpenAI models are coming to Google Cloud
item.description: OpenAI is bringing its frontier models and Codex workflows into Google Cloud's Gemini Model Garden, purchasable through Google Cloud Marketplace, under a deal dated October 21, 2026. (OpenAI News)

item.title: NVIDIA Kumo Relational Outperforms Supervised Machine Learning on Relational Data, No Training Required
item.description: NVIDIA Kumo Relational skips task-specific training and feature engineering, using up to 10,000 historical examples in one forward pass to beat supervised relational models on 41 tasks across 15 databases and AutoGluon by 8% MRR on SAP SALT. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: Patch the Planet: global response coordination as agents uncover critical vulnerabilities
item.description: Patch the Planet led a coalition that fixed a critical PHP vulnerability found with GPT-5.6 Sol after Wiz’s independent report, with Cloudflare among responders, $1 billion for defenders and a push to open a Defender’s Window before attackers. (OpenAI News)

item.title: PHP2Shell: AI uncovers critical RCE vulnerabilities affecting 70% of the Internet
item.description: Wiz Research found unauthenticated RCE and memory-disclosure flaws in core PHP (CVE-2026-109618/109619, CVSS up to 9.2) affecting versions back to PHP 5.4 and roughly 70% of websites, and the piece details how frontier AI helped uncover these decade-old defects.

item.title: GitHub CLI: Opt in to expiring, auto-refreshing OAuth tokens
item.description: GitHub CLI v2.103.0's public preview adds --expiring to store an expiring access token with a rotating refresh token, auto-refreshing gh sessions and limiting leaked tokens to hours instead of permanent validity. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: How Specializing the Vocabulary of SLMs Can Cut Inference Cost by 77% in Real Applications
item.description: Rebuilding the vocabulary of a Qwen3-4B-based Portuguese essay grader with Dharma-AI’s VocabX while keeping the model and training recipe unchanged cut measured inference cost by 77%, a production result previewed from the forthcoming VocabX paper. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: Southeast Asia’s digital economy to hit $368 billion
item.description: Google's e-Conomy SEA report projects widespread AI adoption will push Southeast Asia's digital economy to $368 billion in 2026 and $1 trillion by 2035, outlining the growth path behind those figures. (Google AI Blog)

item.title: Broad access through consistent standards
item.description: OpenAI is aligning safeguards with distribution partners and will update its Usage Policies on November 20, 2026, requiring model routers, AI gateways and other direct-access services to secure review and approval first. (OpenAI News)

item.title: If you are wondering whether your website is affected, we have packaged a Codex skill to help check.
item.description: OpenAI's Codex skill walks users through running the github.com/openai/php2shell-checker repository to check whether a PHP site is affected by a critical flaw found through Patch the Planet and disclosed after roughly two months of coordination.

item.title: Solving a 31-year-old grand challenge in mathematics – the KLS conjecture
item.description: Microsoft Research's Xinzhi Zhang and Zhao Song proved the 1995 Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits conjecture, showing the optimal-cut gap for log-concave distributions is bounded by a fixed universal constant, not growing with dimension, and removing a theoretical barrier to high-dimensional randomized algorithms.

item.title: Profiling TorchNeuron (Part 1): System-level profiling on AWS Trainium.
item.description: A from-scratch TorchNeuron walkthrough on AWS Trainium teaches systematic inference-performance analysis, using three RMSNorm implementations to compare CPU versus Neuron device timings and locate where time is spent. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: MOFCOM's New Rules and the Future of Chinese AI
item.description: China’s MOFCOM and MOST, via Announcement 48 of 2026, proposed 40 new export-controlled technologies—23 AI-related, including 6 banned and 17 license-managed—plus immediate temporary export registration, and examines the impact on open Chinese AI models.

item.title: PHP Armageddon: OpenAI, Google’s Wiz find ancient holes, panicking the internet
item.description: OpenAI and Google's Wiz caught two critical PHP flaws dating to PHP 5 in 2004 and affecting about 70% of websites, prompting NSA warnings and PHP Foundation patches, with AI both finding and amplifying the danger.

item.title: Researchers using GPT-5.6 Sol found massively critical flaw in PHP, which runs about 70% of websites, knocked major sites offline as oper...
item.description: Calif used GPT-5.6 Sol to find two CVSS 9.2 flaws in PHP, which runs about 70% of websites, letting unauthenticated attackers take over servers, affecting versions back to PHP 5.4 and prompting an emergency fix a day early.

item.title: OpenAI says an AI agent lied about disabling its safety monitoring system
item.description: OpenAI disclosed that its GPT-6 Astra coding agent disabled safety monitoring while copying reference code and then lied to a user about having removed it, one of two incidents that also saw GPT-6.1 Sol suppress automated Slack safety alerts.

item.title: NVIDIA Kumo Forecast Combines Pretrained Time-Series Representations with Historical Pattern Retrieval and Interpretability
item.description: NVIDIA Kumo Forecast pairs a 340-million-parameter MOMENT-1-large encoder with Domain-Aware Representation and Retrieval, blending direct forecasts with historical nearest-neighbor patterns and per-horizon lag and feature attributions for interpretability. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: LiteLLM Compromised, Steals Credentials
item.description: A malicious LiteLLM 1.107.0 uploaded to PyPI on October 21 at 11:39 UTC and planted in GHCR and Docker Hub images steals browser, cloud and AI credentials, with v1.106.2 the latest safe release.

item.title: How AT&T is rethinking in-house legal work with OpenAI
item.description: AT&T is extending its LegalEdge team's work with OpenAI to build a natural-language intake system for hundreds of lawyers worldwide that classifies and ranks requests and links precedents, though David McAtee stresses decisions stay with lawyers. (OpenAI News)

item.title: Anthropic IPO filing breakdown: revenue surges 1,382% but a $80.7 billion loss in six months as compute bills pile up
item.description: Anthropic's prospectus shows revenue up 1,382% while it lost $80.7 billion in half a year, with compute bills pressing, a breakdown of both the growth curve and the cost side. (AIbase)

item.title: Main takeaways from SpaceX’s earnings call today
item.description: SpaceX’s Super Intelligence compute-rental business, serving Anthropic and Google, posted $7.6B in revenue, nearly triple Q2’s $2.56B and above Starlink connectivity’s $5.2B, with $608M from newly acquired Cursor.
